newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bonn's Stark-no need to alter 2.9 pct deficit goal.
newsitem.headline: Bonn's Stark-no need to alter 2.9 pct deficit goal.

text.p: German state secretary in the finance ministry Juergen Stark said on Thursday that there was no need for the German government to alter its 1997 budget deficit forecast after March jobs numbers.
The jobs data, released on Tuesday, showed a 15,000 fall in unemployment to a seasonally adjusted 4.30 million in March.
The government's forecast is for Germany's budget deficit to total 2.9 percent of gross domestic product in 1997. "That (forecast) remains in place after the latest labour market data," Stark said.
